text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices surged on escalating geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, pushing U.S. crude oil prices sharply higher—Brent crude touched $110 a barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices translate directly to higher revenue and profits, which is why the stock has climbed 15.6% over the past two weeks as regional tensions have mounted.

The move also reflects a growing recognition among traders that the "true" cost of oil is higher than the headline price suggests: physical delivery costs have surged due to elevated tanker rates, adding roughly $30–$40 per barrel to the actual cost of getting oil to market. This squeeze on supply logistics, combined with the supply concerns from Middle East instability, has kept upward pressure on crude prices and benefited producers.
